account: Extracted eight anchored findings from the enclosed Du et al. text covering claimed gains (reasoning and factuality), experimental setup (agents, rounds, tasks, consensus mechanism), and stated limitations. All findings carry the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers. The source file was fully enclosed, so the findings are direct quotes or close paraphrases from the text.

citations.excerpt: Our findings indicate that this approach significantly enhances mathematical and strategic reasoning across a number of tasks.

claims.statement: The paper claims that multiagent debate significantly enhances mathematical and strategic reasoning across a variety of tasks.

citations.excerpt: We also demonstrate that our approach improves the factual validity of generated content, reducing fallacious answers and hallucinations that contemporary models are prone to.

claims.statement: The paper claims the debate approach improves the factual validity of generated content, reducing fallacious answers and hallucinations.

citations.excerpt: Due to computational expense, we evaluate our approach across benchmarks mainly using three agents with two rounds of debates, although we found further gains with both more agents and rounds of debate (Figure 10).

claims.statement: The main benchmark evaluations used three agents with two rounds of debate, though further gains were found with more agents and rounds.
The reasoning tasks were arithmetic, GSM8K grade-school math, and chess move prediction; factuality tasks were biographies, MMLU, and chess move validity.

citations.excerpt: Individual responses from other agents are concatenated and given as context to each agent, with each agent instructed to construct a new response based on such responses. ... We iteratively repeat this debate procedure over multiple rounds for improved performance.

claims.statement: The debate procedure: agents generate initial answers, then each agent reads the responses of all other agents, which are concatenated into a prompt, and each agent updates its answer; this is repeated over multiple rounds.

citations.excerpt: After debating and examining the responses of other model instances, we find that the population almost always converges on a single and more accurate common answer.

claims.statement: The paper states that after multiple rounds, the population almost always converges on a single, more accurate common answer.

citations.excerpt: our multiagent debate procedure is more computationally expensive, as it requires both multiple language generations, and an underlying debate procedure.

claims.statement: The authors state the debate procedure is more computationally expensive than other prompting techniques, requiring multiple language generations and the underlying debate procedure.

citations.excerpt: we found that while debates typically converged into single final answers, these answers were not necessarily correct. Despite answers being incorrect, language models would confidently affirm that their answer is correct and consistent with all other agent responses.

claims.statement: The authors observed that although debates typically converge to a single final answer, that answer is not necessarily correct, and language models will confidently affirm incorrect answers as consistent with all other agent responses.

objective: Extract from papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt, each anchored to the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s), at least four findings that cover: (a) the improvements in factuality and reasoning the paper claims for multiagent debate, (b) the experimental setup (number of agents, number of debate rounds, tasks used, and how consensus/final answer is reached), and (c) any limitations the authors state. Return each finding as a quote or close paraphrase with the exact page marker(s).
